mission: Write a short announcement to my engineering team that we are moving to a weekly on-call rotation. The goal is for the team to accept the change and know exactly what it means for them; many are frustrated about pager load, so the message must show how this change addresses that.
provisions: - Audience: my direct team of backend engineers who currently share on-call ad hoc. - Change: weekly rotation starting [START DATE]; handoff at [HANDOFF DAY/TIME]; schedule lives at [SCHEDULE LINK]; escalation path is [ESCALATION CONTACT]. - Known concern: pager load feels unpredictable and unevenly shared. - Sender: me, the team lead. Perspective: a lead who has heard the complaints and is fixing a process, not defending one.
scope: - Use only the facts above; keep every bracketed placeholder exactly as written. - Acknowledge the frustration in one sentence, then move to specifics. - Avoid promising outcomes I have not stated (for example, fewer total pages).
success_spec: Output: a subject line, then a message of 150–250 words in plain, direct language, ending with one clear call to action (check your first shift date at [SCHEDULE LINK] and raise conflicts by [DEADLINE]). Before returning, check: (1) every placeholder is preserved, (2) the pager-load concern is addressed explicitly, (3) no unstated promises appear.
